rawIssues.issue: apiVersion '2023-05-03' predates the 2025-02-19 change that made 'published' the default perspective. On older versions the default is 'raw', so queries made with the read token can return draft documents alongside published ones, which can leak unpublished content or produce duplicates. Set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly, or bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or later after checking the other behavior changes.

projectId and dataset come from process.env and are typed `string | undefined`, with no validation or assertion. A missing variable fails at runtime with an unclear error and may not type-check. Add a helper that throws if a variable is missing.

A single shared client has `useCdn: false` and a token. Public published-content fetches therefore bypass the API CDN and pay for uncached requests. Consider a separate CDN-enabled client without a token for public reads, and keep the token-bearing client for draft mode and preview only.

The token is read from SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN, which is correctly not NEXT_PUBLIC_, but it lives in a client module that may be imported from client components. That would either fail with an undefined token or tempt someone to expose it. Mark the file `server-only` or split server and browser clients.

No `stega` or `studioUrl` configuration is set, so Visual Editing and click-to-edit overlays will not work in draft mode. Also, with no explicit perspective, preview and draft handling is ambiguous. Configure `perspective: 'drafts'` (or 'previewDrafts' on older versions) only for draft-mode fetches.
Missing `apiVersion`. The client falls back to the legacy default API version (v1) and logs a warning, so behavior can change unexpectedly. Pin an explicit date such as '2025-02-19'.

No `perspective` is set. For apiVersion before 2025-02-19 the default perspective is `raw`, so queries can return both draft and published documents (including `drafts.` IDs). From 2025-02-19 the default is `published`. Set `perspective` explicitly (e.g. 'published') to get consistent results.

A token is configured on a shared, exported client. If this module is imported in browser code, the token will be bundled and leaked. Keep authenticated clients server-only, use a read-only token if writes are not needed, and use a separate tokenless client with `useCdn: true` for public reads.

`useCdn: false` combined with a token means every request hits the live API, which is slower and higher cost. That is fine for fresh or draft reads but should be intentional. Public published content should use the CDN with a tokenless client.

The file is TypeScript but uses CommonJS `require`/`module.exports`, which loses type information and mixes module systems. Use `import { createClient } from '@sanity/client'` and `export const client = createClient(...)`.
`process.env.SANITY_TOKEN` is not validated. If it is undefined the client silently runs unauthenticated, and private datasets or drafts will fail with confusing errors. Fail fast when it is missing.
perspective 'previewDrafts' is deprecated and has been renamed to 'drafts'. Newer API versions (v2025-02-19 and later) use 'drafts', so update both the perspective and the apiVersion.

useCdn: true conflicts with a draft-reading perspective and an authenticated token. Draft content is not served reliably from the CDN, and token-authenticated requests should not go through it, so preview/draft content may be stale or missing. Set useCdn: false for the preview client.

apiVersion '2022-11-15' is pinned to an old date. Since 2025-02-19 the default perspective is 'published' instead of 'raw', so behavior will change when you upgrade. Pin a recent date deliberately and test the perspective semantics.

The preview token is read from process.env with no check that it exists. If it is undefined, the client silently falls back to unauthenticated requests and draft documents are not returned. Fail fast if the token is missing, and never expose this token to browser bundles. Use it only server-side, or use a viewer-scoped token.

The `id` param is passed to `fetch` but the query never references `$id`. The query returns the first draft post it finds, not the draft with that ID, so `getDraft(id)` returns the wrong document. Filter on `_id == 'drafts.' + $id` or `_id == $draftId`, and pass the param under the name the query uses.

The query relies on the default perspective including drafts (`raw`). That default applies only to API versions before 2025-02-19. From 2025-02-19 the default perspective is `published`, so `drafts.**` documents are excluded and the query returns null. Set `perspective` explicitly (`raw` or `drafts`) and don't depend on the apiVersion default.
`useCdn` is not set. Draft and authenticated reads must not go through the CDN, since drafts are not served by the APICDN and a token is ignored there. Set `useCdn: false` explicitly for this client.

The apiVersion `2021-10-21` is old, and a hard-coded old date means you miss newer query and perspective behavior. Pin a recent date deliberately and review the changelog. Upgrading past 2025-02-19 will change the default perspective and break this draft query unless a perspective is set.
`[0]` is used without `order()`, so which draft is returned is non-deterministic. Add an ordering such as `| order(_updatedAt desc)` before `[0]`.

A read/write `token` is passed from `process.env.SANITY_TOKEN`. If this module is bundled for the browser, the token leaks. Keep the token server-side only, use a read-only Viewer token for drafts, and use a separate token-less client for public reads.
The `client` is not exported and the `id` parameter has no type, so it is an implicit `any` under TypeScript strict mode. Type it as `id: string` and export the client for reuse.

The projection `"": author->{name, image}` uses an empty-string key, which is invalid GROQ or produces a nonsensical result. Use a named key such as `author->{name, image}` or `"author": author->{name, image}`.

The `slug` parameter of `getPost` has no type, so it is an implicit `any` under strict TypeScript. Type it as `string`, and give the function a return type or use typed GROQ (for example with `defineQuery` and TypeGen).

The apiVersion '2024-06-01' is pinned before 2025-02-19. From that version the default perspective becomes 'published' (it was 'raw') and 'previewDrafts' is renamed 'drafts'. The explicit `perspective: 'published'` hides the difference for this client, but other code on this apiVersion, or code that omits the perspective, will behave differently. Consider updating the apiVersion and testing the queries.

`image` is projected without dereferencing its asset (for example `image{..., asset->}`), so it returns only an asset reference. A URL builder can handle that, but direct URL access needs the dereferenced asset.

`useCdn: true` together with `perspective: 'published'` is fine for public content. The CDN may serve slightly stale data, so don't use this client for previews or draft content. Use a separate client with a token and `useCdn: false` for those.
There is no error handling or null handling. `[0]` returns null when no post matches the slug, so callers must handle null and fetch failures.

The pinned apiVersion '2023-08-01' is older than 2025-02-19, so queries default to the 'raw' perspective. That can return both draft and published documents, including duplicates. From 2025-02-19 the default is 'published'. Either bump the version and verify behavior, or set `perspective` explicitly.
The `client` returned by useClient is never used. No query, fetch or listener runs, so the hook call has no effect.
RelatedPosts always returns null and renders nothing. The related-posts logic (GROQ query, loading and error state, rendering) is missing.

No GROQ query, document-ID or reference input, or data-fetching lifecycle (useEffect, state, cleanup) is defined. Any data fetch added later should run in an effect, with the client's `fetch` called inside it rather than during render.

The GROQ function sanity::versionOf() is not available at apiVersion 2024-03-01. It requires API version 2025-02-19 or later (the content releases/versions support), so the query will fail or be rejected. Bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or newer.

client.listen() returns a subscription that is never unsubscribed. This leaks a live connection on every render and unmount. It should be created in a useEffect and the subscription cleaned up in the effect's return.

client.fetch() and client.listen() are called directly in the render body, which is a side effect on every render. The fetch result is discarded and its promise is unhandled (no catch). Move both into useEffect or a data hook and store the result in state.

The listener filter *[_id == $id] only matches the exact document ID. It will not match draft (drafts.<id>) or version (versions.<release>.<id>) documents, so it can miss changes that the versionOf count covers. Listen on a filter that covers those variants, such as sanity::versionOf($id) (needs 2025-02-19+) or explicit ID patterns.

The useClient instance is recreated on every render and the apiVersion is hard-coded and inconsistent with the features used. Memoize the client or use a shared constant API version. The props destructuring `{id}` also has no type annotation, so it is implicitly any under strict TypeScript.
client.listen() returns a lazy Observable and nothing subscribes to it, so no listener connection is ever opened and the call does nothing. Call .subscribe() and unsubscribe on cleanup.

The listener is created in the component render body, so it is a side effect that runs on every render. Move it into useEffect with a cleanup that unsubscribes, otherwise subscriptions leak and duplicate.
useClient(...).withConfig(...) builds a new client on every render. Memoize it with useMemo, or create it once outside the component.

The perspective is explicitly set to 'raw'. 'raw' was the default before apiVersion 2025-02-19, and from that version the default is 'published'. Setting 'raw' keeps the legacy behavior and returns drafts, published documents and release versions mixed together, which is wrong for a release tool. Use 'drafts', or a specific release or perspective stack, unless raw access is truly needed.

includeAllVersions on listen() is an experimental option that is not available on the stable dated API version used here ('2025-02-19'). It requires the experimental 'vX' apiVersion, so the option may be ignored or rejected. Use a dedicated client with apiVersion 'vX' for this listener, or drop the option.

The listen query, '*[_type == "post"]', is unfiltered and has no projection. It will receive events for every post, and for every version (draft, published, release) when includeAllVersions is on. Narrow the filter and handle events by document ID, and note that a 'raw' perspective makes the version events harder to tell apart.

The function is named useWatch like a React hook, but it just returns a raw RxJS Observable from client.listen(). Nothing subscribes to it and nothing unsubscribes on unmount, so the listener connection can leak. Subscribe inside useEffect and return a cleanup that calls subscription.unsubscribe().

The client and id parameters are untyped, so the code relies on implicit any. Type client as SanityClient and id as string. The client must also be created with an explicit apiVersion (a dated YYYY-MM-DD string) and useCdn set to false, because listening does not work through the CDN.

The filter '*[_id == $id]' matches only the exact ID. If id is a published ID, changes to the draft (drafts.<id>) won't be received, and the reverse is also true. Listen to both IDs, for example '*[_id in [$id, "drafts." + $id]]', or normalize the ID first.

includeResult: true makes every event carry the full document, which wastes bandwidth on large documents and on frequent edits. The option is also redundant, since the full result is already the default in recent client versions. Prefer the default mendoza effectFormat (the event's effects field) with includeResult: false if you only need to know that a change happened, or fetch the document separately after an event.

There is no error or reconnect handling, and no initial fetch. The listener only emits changes made after it connects, so the current document value is never delivered. Do a client.fetch() for the initial state, handle the 'welcome', 'reconnect', 'mutation' and 'disconnect' events, and add an error callback on subscribe.

No visibility option is set. The default 'sync' is fine for most cases, but if you re-fetch after an event, use visibility: 'query' so the following fetch sees the change. With 'sync' there is a race between the event arriving and the document being queryable.

`perspective: 'published'` is redundant with this apiVersion. Since API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is 'published' (it was 'raw' before), so you can drop the explicit setting. If you ever pin an apiVersion before that date, the explicit value becomes necessary to avoid draft documents being returned.
apiVersion '2026-09-01' may be a future or unvetted date. Pin a real, tested date, or use a 'vX' experimental version only deliberately, so query behavior stays predictable.
The `createClient` import from '@sanity/client' or 'next-sanity' is missing, so the snippet won't compile on its own.

`useCdn: true` serves cached content, which can be slightly stale. Use `useCdn: false` for server-side fetches that need fresh data, in draft or preview mode, or when using a token. The apiCdn is only suitable for published content.
projectId and dataset are hardcoded. Prefer environment variables, so the same code works across dev, staging and production datasets.

`perspective: 'published'` is redundant. From API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is already `published` (previously `raw`). Setting it explicitly is harmless, and it makes the intent clear for older versions.

The `drafts` perspective (the renamed `previewDrafts`) only exists from API version 2025-02-19. It works with apiVersion 2025-10-01, but it would fail or need the old `previewDrafts` name if the apiVersion were pinned lower.

`previewClient` reads a token from `process.env.SANITY_VIEWER_TOKEN` in the same module as the public client. If this module is imported in client-side code, the token can leak into the browser bundle. Move the preview client to a server-only module, and avoid `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-style env vars for the token.
`previewClient` has no `stega` config (`stega: {enabled: true, studioUrl}`) for visual editing or click-to-edit overlays. Add it if the preview is meant to support Presentation or Visual Editing.

The token is only attached to `previewClient`, which is correct. If `token` is undefined because the env var is missing, the `drafts` perspective silently returns no draft content, so validate that the env var is set at startup.
`createClient` is not imported. Add `import {createClient} from '@sanity/client'` or `from 'next-sanity'`.

An array perspective (a release stack such as ['rSummer', 'drafts']) is only supported on API version 2025-02-19 or later. 2025-03-01 satisfies this, so there is no bug now. Do not lower apiVersion below the boundary, or the stack will be rejected or ignored.
The perspective value 'drafts' replaced the older 'previewDrafts' name from 2025-02-19 onward. Using 'drafts' is correct here, but it would not be valid on older API versions.

The client has a token and reads draft and release content. If this module is imported into browser code, the token is bundled and exposed. Keep it server-only, or create a separate tokenless client for public use.

useCdn: false is correct for a perspective that reads unpublished release and draft content, because the CDN does not serve it. Make sure nobody switches it to true. The cost is uncached, slower, and rate-limited requests, so use this client only for preview or release-preview routes.

The release ID 'rSummer' is hard-coded. It breaks when the release is archived, published, or deleted, and the stack then silently returns different content. Load the release ID from config or an environment variable. The name 'releaseClient' also suggests it should be scoped to preview use only.

The perspective stack is order-sensitive and 'published' is implicit at the end, so check that the order puts the release ahead of drafts as you intend. Raw or other single-name perspectives cannot be mixed into the array.

apiVersion is computed dynamically from today's date. This defeats API versioning, because every day you silently opt into the newest behavior and any breaking change can alter query results without a code change. It also changes the CDN request URL each day, which hurts cache hit rates. Pin a fixed, reviewed date string such as '2025-02-19' and upgrade deliberately.

Because the version floats to the latest date, the default perspective is 'published' (drafts excluded) rather than the older 'raw' (drafts and published mixed). Behavior differs depending on whether the effective date is before or after 2025-02-19. Code written against 'raw' results, such as expecting drafts. will silently change. Set `perspective` explicitly and pin the version.

useCdn: true is set unconditionally. The CDN can serve slightly stale data and cannot be used for authenticated or draft/preview requests. For previews, drafts, server-side rendering that needs fresh data, or ISR revalidation or webhook-driven fetches, use a separate client with useCdn: false and a token. Consider setting it from the environment, for example `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`.
projectId and dataset are hardcoded rather than read from environment variables. This makes it harder to use different projects or datasets for staging and production, and it invites config drift.

With a read token and an apiVersion before 2025-02-19, the default perspective is 'raw'. Queries can then return draft documents and duplicates alongside published ones. Set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly, and use 'drafts' or 'previewDrafts' only in preview mode with a token. From 2025-02-19 the default becomes 'published', but relying on that default is fragile.
The fallback apiVersion '2023-06-21' is old. It misses the newer default-perspective behavior and other API changes. Pin a recent fixed date and upgrade deliberately after testing.
apiVersion is read from an environment variable at runtime, so different environments can silently run with different API behavior. Hardcode a single pinned date in the config instead.

projectId and dataset are hardcoded. Move them to environment variables (for example NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET) so staging and production can differ, and validate that they are set.

useCdn is false for all queries, which gives up the faster, cached API CDN for published content. Use `useCdn: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`, or keep a separate non-CDN client with the token for previews and drafts. The CDN is not used with drafts or tokens anyway.

The token is attached to the shared client. If this client is imported into client-side code, the token is undefined in the browser. If it were ever exposed through NEXT_PUBLIC_*, it would leak. Keep the authenticated client server-only, and use a tokenless client for public published reads.
The snippet does not import createClient from '@sanity/client' or 'next-sanity'. It also has no `stega` or `perspective` configuration, which preview and visual editing setups need.

apiVersion comes from process.env.SANITY_API_VERSION, which may be undefined at runtime or at build time. The client then falls back to the legacy v1 API and logs a warning, and behavior can differ between environments. Pin a fixed date string such as '2025-02-19' in code.

perspective: 'raw' returns both draft and published documents, including duplicates with drafts. and versions. prefixed IDs, so queries need manual filtering. The default perspective changed from 'raw' to 'published' at API version 2025-02-19, so 'raw' is now an explicit opt-out of the safer default. Use 'published' for production content, or 'drafts' (formerly 'previewDrafts') for previews.

A token is set on a shared exported client. If this module is imported in browser-side code, the token leaks into the bundle. Keep authenticated clients server-only, use a read-only token, and create a separate token-less client for public use.

useCdn: false means every request goes to the uncached API. That is only needed for fresh or draft reads. For published content in production, useCdn: true gives lower latency and cost, with a separate non-CDN client for previews. Note that a token combined with the CDN bypasses the cache.

apiVersion '2023-05-03' is before 2025-02-19, so the default perspective is `raw`. `raw` returns drafts and published documents side by side, unmerged. With a read token that can see drafts, queries can return duplicate documents (`drafts.*` and published) and leak unpublished content to production pages. Set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly for production, or bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or later, where `published` is the default. If you bump, also check for code that relied on the old `raw` default.

Content Releases features are unavailable on this pinned version. Release-ID perspective stacks, `includeAllVersions` on listen and doc, `sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease` and `releases::all()` need apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later. `versions.**` documents are also not returned on earlier versions. Bump the version before using releases or release previews.

At 2025-02-19 and later, an empty-string key (`""`) in a GROQ projection no longer expands into the parent object. Before that, it did. The current version still has the old behavior, so any query that relies on it needs the `...` spread when you bump.

`useCdn: false` sends every read to the uncached API (`api.sanity.io`). That is fine for previews, drafts perspective and static builds. For production frontend reads with the `published` perspective, `useCdn: true` is recommended. It gives lower latency, scales without hitting direct-API rate and concurrency limits (CDN hits aren't rate limited), and the client has fetched from the CDN with a token since @sanity/client v3. Use separate clients or config: CDN on for published reads, CDN off for preview, drafts or release stacks.

One client is used for everything, with a read token and no explicit `perspective`. Preview and draft use should be separate: a `drafts` or release-stack perspective with `useCdn: false`, using the token only on the server. Production should use `published`. Keep the token server-only; it is correctly not `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.

`projectId` and `dataset` come from `process.env` with no fallback or assertion, so they can be `undefined` at runtime. Validate them and fail early. The apiVersion is a static literal, which is correct.

`apiVersion` is missing. The JS client logs a deprecation warning and defaults to the outdated `v1` API. Set a static literal date string such as '2026-07-28'. Don't compute it with `new Date()`, because that changes the pinned version every day.

Because there is no `apiVersion`, the client runs on `v1` and queries default to the `raw` perspective. That returns drafts and published documents side by side, so draft content can leak into the results. From `v2025-02-19` the default perspective is `published`, and `raw` also includes `versions.**` documents. When you add an `apiVersion`, set `perspective` explicitly ('published' for production, or 'raw'/'drafts' if you need the old behavior). Also check any code that matches on `drafts.` path prefixes.

`useCdn: false` combined with a `token` means every read goes straight to the live API. That is correct for guaranteed-fresh data, such as previews with the `drafts` perspective. For production published-content reads it gives up CDN latency and caching benefits. Consider `useCdn: true` with the `published` perspective. Since `@sanity/client` v3.0.0, a token together with `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN. Before v3 the token forced a CDN bypass.

`useCdn: true` is used together with the `previewDrafts` perspective. The drafts perspective is not cached by the CDN, so the client bypasses the CDN and logs a warning. Set `useCdn: false` for this preview client.
`previewDrafts` is the old name for the `drafts` perspective. It still works, but the docs say `drafts` is preferred. Switch to `perspective: 'drafts'`.

`apiVersion: '2022-11-15'` is older than `2025-02-19`. At that version, `versions.**` documents are not returned, and release-based perspective stacks and the `includeAllVersions` parameter on `/listen` and `/doc` are unavailable. Content Releases previews would need a bump. Also, the default perspective was `raw` before this date and is `published` from it onward. The explicit perspective setting avoids that default change. Bump the version in small steps and test.

A preview token is combined with `useCdn: true`. Since @sanity/client v3.0.0, a token plus `useCdn: true` fetches from the CDN instead of bypassing it. A preview or draft-capable token should not be paired with the CDN. Authenticated requests are cached per token. The preview client should use `useCdn: false` so it gets fresh data.

The query filters on `_id in path("drafts.**")` and only works because the pinned apiVersion (2021-10-21) still defaults to the `raw` perspective. From v2025-02-19 the default perspective is `published`, which excludes drafts, so this query returns nothing once the version is bumped. The same bump makes `raw` include `versions.**` documents. Set the perspective explicitly (`perspective: 'drafts'` or `'raw'`) instead of relying on the implicit default and on path-prefix matching. With `drafts`, set `useCdn: false`.

Path-prefix matching on `drafts.**` is the wrong way to read drafts. The docs recommend using perspectives to control which documents are returned. The `drafts` perspective overlays drafts onto published documents and adds `_originalId`. It isn't CDN-cached, so `useCdn` must be `false`, otherwise the client bypasses the CDN and logs a warning.

The pinned apiVersion '2021-10-21' is old. It predates the Content Releases and perspective changes in v2025-02-19, so `versions.*` documents are not returned and release perspectives and the new GROQ functions are unavailable. Bump it deliberately to a static date string, after reading the changelog and testing, and prefer several small upgrades over one large jump.

The `{id}` parameter is passed to `fetch`, but the GROQ query never references `$id`. As written, `getDraft(id)` ignores its argument and returns the first post draft, and `[0]` has no `order()`, so the result is not deterministic. To fetch one draft, filter by `_id == $id`, or by `_id == 'drafts.' + $id` if you want the draft only, rather than hard-coding the path filter.

The client reads drafts with a token but doesn't set `useCdn` or `perspective`. Drafts require an authenticated request, and the docs say that from @sanity/client v3.0.0, passing a token with `useCdn: true` uses the CDN. Draft or preview reads should explicitly set `useCdn: false`. Keep the token server-side only.

The projection key `"": author->{name, image}` uses an empty-string key. At the pinned apiVersion 2024-06-01 it silently spreads the dereferenced author's fields into the parent object. From v2025-02-19 the API fixed this bug, so the key no longer expands and the result shape changes. Bumping apiVersion later would silently break this query. Replace it with the explicit spread `...author->{name, image}`, which works on both sides of the boundary.

apiVersion 2024-06-01 is older than v2025-02-19. At this version the default perspective is still `raw`, and `versions.**` documents are not returned. The explicit `perspective: 'published'` is correct and protects against draft leakage, so keep it when you bump. Release-based perspectives and the newer GROQ functions (`sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease`, `releases::all`) are not available at this version.

apiVersion '2023-08-01' is before 2025-02-19, so queries from this client default to the `raw` perspective. `raw` returns drafts and published documents side by side, unmerged. That can surface `drafts.*` duplicates in a component like RelatedPosts. From 2025-02-19 the default is `published`. Set `perspective` explicitly, or bump the version after reviewing the changelog and testing.

At this pinned version, `versions.**` (Content Release) documents are not returned. Release-based perspective stacks, `includeAllVersions` on `/listen` and `/doc`, and the `sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease` and `releases::all()` GROQ functions are also unavailable. Anything that targets Content Releases, including Studio plugins, needs apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later.

If you bump to 2025-02-19 or later, also check the other breaking changes at that boundary. The `raw` perspective will include `versions.**` documents, so path-prefix checks for `drafts.` may behave unexpectedly. An empty-string key (`""`) in a GROQ projection no longer expands into the parent object. Use the `...` spread operator if you relied on the old behavior. Bump deliberately and test, rather than computing the date at runtime.

`sanity::versionOf()` needs apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later. At the pinned '2024-03-01' the function isn't available, so the count query will not work. Bump apiVersion to '2025-02-19' or later. The function also expects a published document ID, not a `drafts.` or `versions.` ID.

No `perspective` is set, so the result depends on the apiVersion. At '2024-03-01' the default is `raw`, which returns drafts and published documents unmerged. From 2025-02-19 the default becomes `published`, which excludes drafts and versions. After a bump, `count(*[sanity::versionOf($id)])` would then count only the published document. Set `perspective: 'raw'` explicitly to count all versions. Version documents are not returned at all on API versions before 2025-02-19.

`client.listen` will not deliver version document changes at '2024-03-01'. The `includeAllVersions` option was added to `/listen` in 2025-02-19, and without it the listener won't receive version or draft changes. Bump the apiVersion and pass `includeAllVersions: true` if the badge needs to react to draft or version edits. The listener filter `*[_id == $id]` only matches the exact published ID.

Side effects run in the component render body. `fetch` and `listen` execute on every render, and the subscription is never unsubscribed, so listeners leak. The fetch result is discarded and the promise has no error handling. Move both into `useEffect`, store the result in state, and return a cleanup that calls `subscription.unsubscribe()`.

`useCdn` is not set, and the client is created with `useClient` on every render with no stated perspective or CDN intent. Release and draft content is never served from the CDN, so a client that reads drafts or versions should set `useCdn: false`.

`client.listen(...)` is called directly in the component render body. Every re-render opens a new listener, and the listener is never cleaned up. It should be set up in a `useEffect` and torn down when the component unmounts. This is general React/client practice. The retrieved docs don't cover it.

The result of `client.listen()` is never subscribed to or stored. `listen` returns an observable, so nothing is received without `.subscribe()`. There is also no handle to call `.unsubscribe()` on. The retrieved docs don't cover this. It comes from general knowledge of the client.

`includeAllVersions: true` on `/listen` only exists from API version 2025-02-19. The pinned '2025-02-19' is exactly the minimum, so it works now. Lowering or changing the pin would silently drop the option and version/draft changes. The option also needs an authenticated request, and the code configures no token. In a Studio the `useClient` client normally carries the user's session, but this is not covered in the docs I retrieved. Content Releases and version documents also require Enterprise, and an `@sanity/client` of 7.8.0 or later.

`perspective: 'raw'` is set explicitly, which is correct because the default became `published` at 2025-02-19. At this version, though, `raw` also returns `versions.**` documents alongside `drafts.**` and published ones. Any code that checks `drafts.` ID prefixes will see unexpected version documents. The `post` results and listener events may include the same post as published, draft and version copies. Prefer a `drafts` perspective or a release stack where possible, and handle `versions.*` IDs, for example with `@sanity/id-utils` or `getPublishedId`. Before 2025-02-19, `raw` was the implicit default and had no `versions.**` documents.

I found nothing in the docs showing that the `perspective` set via `withConfig` applies to `listen`. The docs describe `perspective` for queries. Don't rely on it to control which document states the listener delivers. That is controlled by `includeAllVersions`.

The query `*[_id == $id]` only matches the exact ID you pass. Drafts (`drafts.<id>`) and versions (`versions.<release>.<id>`) have different `_id` values, so a bare published ID never matches them. From v2025-02-19, `client.listen` needs `includeAllVersions: true` to receive draft and version document changes. Without it, a listener used for editing or preview will miss those changes. If you do want drafts or versions, filter on all the ID forms, for example with `sanity::versionOf()` or `@sanity/id-utils`. The docs I found say only that `includeAllVersions` is needed for draft and version changes. They don't say whether the default listener omits drafts on older versions.

The client's `apiVersion` isn't visible here, because the `client` is passed in. It must be a hardcoded, static date string. If it is omitted, the client warns and defaults to the outdated `v1`. If it is computed from `new Date()`, the pinned version changes daily. Since listener and version behavior changes at v2025-02-19, check that the client is pinned to the version you intend. Plugins targeting Content Releases need `2025-02-19` or later.

The listener shares the client's perspective, which isn't set here. From v2025-02-19 the default perspective changes from `raw` to `published`. Any preview or draft-aware code that relied on the implicit `raw` default may behave differently. Set the perspective explicitly. If you use `drafts` or a release stack, set `useCdn: false`.

No functional problems found. The previewClient correctly sets useCdn: false for the drafts perspective, since drafts results are not CDN-cached and the client warns and bypasses the CDN otherwise. It also supplies a token, which draft access requires. The production client's use of useCdn: true with the published perspective matches the documented best practice. The apiVersion is a static literal date, as the docs recommend.

perspective: 'published' on the base client is redundant at apiVersion 2025-10-01, because published became the default perspective at v2025-02-19. Keeping it is harmless and makes the intent explicit. Note that on any apiVersion before 2025-02-19 the default was raw, so the explicit setting would matter there. Also, previewClient inherits the pinned apiVersion from withConfig, so both clients share the same version.

previewClient holds a token (SANITY_VIEWER_TOKEN). The docs I retrieved only say that drafts and versions are not served to unauthenticated requests. They don't cover token handling, so this is my own caution rather than a documented rule: keep this client server-side only so the token is not bundled into browser code. The docs also say that on the CDN, authenticated requests are cached per token. Here useCdn is false, so the token is not involved in CDN caching.

Perspective order may not be what you intend. In a stack, the leftmost entry has the highest priority. With ['rSummer', 'drafts'], the release versions override drafts, so a draft edit to a document that is also in rSummer will not show. The docs' preview example puts drafts first: ['drafts', 'RELEASE_NAME']. If you want in-progress drafts to win over the release, use ['drafts', 'rSummer']. 'published' is appended automatically, so don't add it.

The apiVersion '2025-03-01' is fine. Release-based perspective stacks need 2025-02-19 or later. On earlier versions only raw, published and drafts are accepted, and a stack returns HTTP 400 ('Complex perspectives are not supported for this version'). Don't lower this version. Also, since 2025-02-19 the default perspective is published and raw includes versions.** documents. Neither affects this client, because the perspective is set explicitly.

Content Releases are an Enterprise-only feature. The docs give a minimum @sanity/client of 7.8.0 for the release APIs. Make sure the installed client is at least that version and the project is on a plan with Releases. Otherwise the release perspective may not work.

The token is named SANITY_VIEWER_TOKEN. Release and draft content needs a token that can read unpublished content, so confirm the token's role can read drafts and release versions. Otherwise you will only see published content or get auth errors. Also make sure the env var is defined at runtime, and keep this client server-side so the token isn't exposed.
